citation: AND-cross-composition: disjoint union of 3-SAT instances — primal treewidth of the union = max over parts, and ∧φ_i is satisfiable iff every φ_i is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: SAT by primal treewidth is FPT (2^tw·poly DP). Disjoint union is a clean AND-cross-composition (parameter = max tw ≤ single-instance size), so no polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard 3-SAT via disjoint union (tw = max; conjunction satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: 3-SAT by treewidth is FPT; same disjoint-union AND-composition as the sat row rules out a poly kernel.

citation: 2k-vertex kernel via Nemhauser–Trotter LP (Math. Programming 1975) / crown decomposition; Chen–Kanj–Xia. Textbook: Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015), ch. 2.
note: Classic 2k-vertex polynomial kernel for Vertex Cover parameterized by solution size k.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard 3-Coloring via disjoint union: tw(union)=max, and the union is 3-colorable iff every component is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly. Cf. BJK's stated result 'Clique parameterized by treewidth admits no poly kernel'.
note: 3-Coloring by treewidth is FPT (3^tw·poly). Disjoint-union AND-composition gives no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly.

citation: Blažej, Choudhary, Knop, Schierreich, Suchý, Valla, 'On Polynomial Kernels for TSP and its Generalizations', IPEC 2022 (arXiv:2207.01109), Lemma 1 + Lemma 57: Hamiltonian Path AND-cross-composes into TSP parameterized by (treewidth + maximum degree); no poly kernel unless PH collapses.
note: TSP/Hamiltonicity is FPT by treewidth (2^O(tw) rank-based/Cut&Count). Lower bound is stated for the larger combined parameter tw+Δ, so a fortiori no poly kernel for treewidth alone (tw ≤ tw+Δ).

citation: Mahajan–Raman, 'Parameterizing above guaranteed values: MaxSat and MaxCut', J. Algorithms 31(2):335–354 (1999): cut ≥ m/2 + k is FPT with a poly (O(k)-edge) kernel. Strengthened above the tighter Edwards–Erdős bound: Crowston–Jones–Mnich (ICALP 2012, Algorithmica) O(k^5); Etscheid–Mnich O(k).
note: Above-m/2 parameterization has a polynomial (indeed linear) kernel.

citation: Thomassé, 'A 4k^2 kernel for feedback vertex set', ACM Trans. Algorithms 6(2):32 (2010).
note: O(k^2)-vertex/edge polynomial kernel for k-FVS.

citation: Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Incompressibility through Colors and IDs', ICALP 2009: Steiner Tree parameterized by (#terminals + solution size) has no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (colors-and-IDs composition).
note: FPT by #terminals (Dreyfus–Wagner 3^ℓ / Björklund et al. 2^ℓ). Lower bound for the larger param (terminals+k) propagates to #terminals alone; no poly kernel.

citation: Bodlaender, Downey, Fellows, Hermelin, 'On problems without polynomial kernels', JCSS 75(8):423–434 (2009): k-Path has no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly via OR-composition (disjoint union of graphs; a k-vertex path lives in one component).
note: Canonical OR-composition example. FPT by color-coding; no polynomial kernel.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard NAE-3-SAT (Schaefer) via disjoint union (tw = max; NAE-satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: NAE-SAT by treewidth is FPT; disjoint-union AND-composition rules out a poly kernel, same convention as sat-3.

parameterization: number of distinct item sizes d
citation: Goemans–Rothvoß (SODA 2014) and Jansen–Klein solve Bin Packing with d distinct sizes in time (log Δ)^(2^(2^d)) — XP (poly for fixed d), explicitly NOT an f(d)·poly FPT algorithm.
note: FPT in the number of distinct item sizes is itself a KNOWN OPEN problem (only XP is known); with FPT unresolved no poly kernel can be claimed. The atlas 'FPT in #distinct item sizes' overstates the literature — hence kernel status open.

parameterization: number of distinct job (processing) types, identical machines
citation: FPT via integer programming in fixed dimension (Lenstra 1983 / Kannan; configuration ILP) — e.g. Cygan et al. (2015) ILP applications. No poly kernel known and no lower bound located for this parameter.
note: Parameter-sensitive: #machines alone is para-NP-hard (NP-hard at m=2, Partition); #job types on related/unrelated machines is para-NP-hard (NP-hard at 6 types); polynomial kernels are known only for the DIFFERENT parameter p_max (Knop et al., 'Scheduling Kernels via Configuration LP', arXiv:2003.02187, ESA 2022). Under the only FPT reading (identical machines, #distinct job types) no poly kernel is known.

citation: Blažej, Choudhary, Knop, Schierreich, Suchý, Valla, IPEC 2022 (arXiv:2207.01109), Lemma 1: Hamiltonian Path AND-cross-composes into TSP parameterized by (treewidth + max degree); no poly kernel unless PH collapses.
note: Same canonical parameter and treatment as the tsp row; lower bound for tw+Δ gives no poly kernel for treewidth alone. (Note: literal metric completion has treewidth n−1; the atlas means the TSP-family problem by input-graph treewidth.)

citation: AND-cross-composition from Holyer's NP-hard 3-edge-coloring of cubic graphs (SICOMP 10(4):718–720, 1981): disjoint union of cubic graphs is cubic (Δ=3), tw = max, and is 3-edge-colorable iff every component is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: Edge-coloring (chromatic index) is FPT by treewidth (Zhou–Nakano–Nishizeki, edge-coloring partial k-trees). Disjoint-union AND-composition on cubic instances rules out a poly kernel.

citation: FPT: Marx, 'Parameterized graph separation problems', Theoret. Comput. Sci. 351(3):394–406 (2006), important separators; O*(2^k) in Cygan et al. Best kernel is 2^O(k); a quasipolynomial kernel k^{(log k)^O(1)} is known (Wahlström, 'Quasipolynomial multicut-mimicking networks and kernelization', ICALP 2020 / arXiv:2002.08825).
note: General (unbounded-terminal) Multiway Cut by solution size: no polynomial kernel is known, and no coNP⊆NP/poly lower bound exists — indeed the quasipolynomial kernel makes one unlikely. Honest FPT-no-poly-known (poly kernels known only for bounded #terminals, O(k^{s+1}), or planar graphs).

citation: Abu-Khzam, 'A quadratic kernel for 3-Set Packing', TAMC 2009 (O(k^2) elements); d-Set Matching has O(k^d)-edge kernels with a matching O(k^{d-ε}) lower bound: Dell–Marx, 'Kernelization of packing problems', SODA 2012.
note: Polynomial (essentially tight) kernel for k-3DM / 3-Set Packing by solution size.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard Positive-1-in-3-SAT (Schaefer) via disjoint union (tw = max; 1-in-3-satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: 1-in-3-SAT by treewidth is FPT; disjoint-union AND-composition rules out a poly kernel (SAT-family convention, same as sat-3/nae-sat).

citation: FPT by treewidth via 2^tw CSP dynamic programming. No poly kernel known; no kernelization lower bound located for MAX-2LIN (or its special case MAX-CUT) parameterized by the treewidth of the instance.
note: As a MAX/threshold problem, disjoint union yields neither a clean AND- nor OR-composition (unlike the satisfy-all CSPs sat-3/nae-sat/1-in-3), so the standard treewidth lower-bound route does not directly apply and no citation was found. The general treewidth heuristic suggests a lower bound likely exists, but it is not citable here — honest FPT-no-poly-known. Distinct from the well-settled above-guarantee Max-Cut (which has a poly kernel).

citation: Chen–Meng, 'A 2k kernel for the cluster editing problem', JCSS 78(1):211–220 (2012); earlier 4k kernel via critical cliques: Guo, 'A more effective linear kernelization for cluster editing', Theoret. Comput. Sci. 410(8–10):718–726 (2009).
note: Linear 2k-vertex polynomial kernel for cluster editing by edit budget k.

citation: AND-cross-composition (Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2014) + AND-distillation lower bound (Drucker, FOCS 2012 / SICOMP 2015)
note: Disjoint union of t planar 3-colouring instances is planar, has treewidth = max_i tw(x_i) ≤ poly(max input size), and is 3-colourable iff ALL components are. That is a valid AND-cross-composition from NP-hard planar 3-colouring, so no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. (Coloring param by treewidth is FPT via 3^tw·n DP.)

citation: Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Kernelization Lower Bounds Through Colors and IDs', ACM Trans. Algorithms 11(2):13 (2014); prelim. ICALP 2009
note: Connected Vertex Cover param by k is one of the flagship no-poly-kernel results proved there via composition (colors-and-IDs). FPT (2^k·n^{O(1)}).

citation: Hagerup, 'Kernels for Edge Dominating Set: Simpler or Smaller', MFCS 2012; cf. Xiao–Kloks–Poon 2013
note: Endpoints of an edge dominating set of size k form a vertex cover of size ≤2k, enabling a kernel with O(k^2) vertices/edges. Poly kernel.

citation: Estivill-Castro, Fellows, Langston, Rosamond, 'FPT is P-time Extremal Structure I' (2005) — 3.75k-vertex kernel; cf. Fellows et al. quadratic kernel
note: Max-Leaf (spanning tree with ≥k leaves) has a linear-vertex kernel (≤3.75k). Poly kernel.

citation: Reduction from Steiner Tree param by #terminals (no poly kernel: Dom–Lokshtanov–Saurabh, ACM TALG 2014 / ICALP 2009)
note: Setting each Steiner terminal's prize to +∞ (>> incident edge costs) makes it a proper potential terminal and forces its inclusion, so Steiner Tree with k terminals = PCStT with |T^+_p|=k. Parameter-preserving, hence no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. FPT in |T^+_p| by the potential-terminals branching.

citation: Bessy, Fomin, Gaspers, Paul, Perez, Saurabh, Thomassé, 'Kernels for feedback arc set in tournaments', JCSS 77 (2011) — (2+ε)k / linear kernel; earlier Dom–Guo–Hüffner–Niedermeier–Truß O(k^2)
note: FAST admits a linear-vertex kernel. Poly kernel (contrast general directed FAS, which is open).

citation: Betzler, Fellows, Guo, Niedermeier, Rosamond, 'Fixed-parameter algorithms for Kemeny rankings', TCS 410 (2009); refined partial kernel Betzler–Bredereck–Niedermeier, JAAMAS 2014
note: Score ≤k bounds total pairwise disagreement by k: ≤O(k) 'dirty' candidates (candidates linear in the score / avg KT-distance) and ≤k deviating votes (identical votes bundled with binary multiplicities). Problem kernel of size poly(k).

citation: Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Kernelization Lower Bounds Through Colors and IDs', ACM Trans. Algorithms 11(2):13 (2014); prelim. ICALP 2009
note: Capacitated Vertex Cover param by k proven to have no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (same colors-and-IDs composition paper). FPT.

parameterization: solution size k (d-Set Packing, set size ≤ d fixed)
citation: Sunflower (Erdős–Rado) kernelization, O(k^d) sets — Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015) ch.2; Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Zehavi, Kernelization (2019)
note: d-Set Packing has an O(k^d)-set sunflower kernel; poly for fixed d. (Color-coding gives the FPT algorithm; the kernel is via sunflowers.) Dell–Marx (SODA 2012): no O(k^{d-ε}) kernel, but poly kernel exists.

citation: Reduction from Steiner Tree param by #terminals (no poly kernel: Dom–Lokshtanov–Saurabh, ACM TALG 2014 / ICALP 2009)
note: A Steiner Tree instance with k terminals = Group Steiner Tree with k singleton groups (parameter-preserving), so no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. FPT in #groups (Dreyfus–Wagner-style DP).

citation: AND-cross-composition (disjoint union) + Drucker AND-distillation lower bound (FOCS 2012 / SICOMP 2015); framework Bodlaender–Downey–Fellows–Hermelin, JCSS 2009
note: Treedepth of a disjoint union = max of components' treedepths, so union has td ≤ k iff all components do — an AND-cross-composition from NP-hard Treedepth. No poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly. Computable in FPT (2^{O(k^2)}·n / linear-FPT) time.

citation: van Bevern, Moser, Niedermeier, 'Kernelization Through Tidying', LATIN 2010 (O(k^2) kernel); CVD is a special case of 3-Hitting Set (hit all induced P3), giving an O(k^2)-vertex kernel
note: Cluster graphs = P3-free, so CVD = 3-Hitting Set on P3-triples → O(k^2)-vertex kernel (O(k^3) weighted). Poly kernel.

citation: Kim, Williams, 'Improved Parameterized Algorithms for Constraint Satisfaction', IPEC 2010 (arXiv:1008.0213) — O(k)-variable bikernels for Boolean CSPs of arity c above average
note: Each arc (u,v) is the arity-2 Boolean constraint x_u∧¬x_v, satisfied with prob 1/4 under a random assignment, so m/4 is exactly the average. 'Above m/4' = Boolean 2-CSP above average → O(k)-variable bikernel; with NP-completeness this yields a polynomial kernel (O(k^2) constraints).

citation: Sunflower-lemma kernel, O(k^d) sets — Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015) ch.2; Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Zehavi, Kernelization (2019); orig. Abu-Khzam 2010
note: The sunflower kernel gives ≤ d!·k^d sets (O(k^{d-1}) improvements known). Textbook poly kernel; Dell–Marx show no O(k^{d-ε}) kernel.

parameterization: number of distinct item sizes d
citation: No kernel or kernel-lower-bound result located for this parameter; even FPT-by-d is not established (Goemans–Rothvoß / Jansen–Klein give (log Δ)^{2^{2^d}}-type XP algorithms, which are not f(d)·poly)
note: Honest open: high-multiplicity/number-problem structure; the row's 'FPT in #distinct sizes' claim rests on XP/quasi-poly algorithms, not an FPT algorithm, so no poly kernel is known (kernel would imply FPT). Could not settle — no establishing R20 citation exists.

citation: Nemhauser–Trotter / crown 2k-vertex kernel (Chen–Kanj–Xia 2010); linear kernel on planar graphs, Alber–Fellows–Niedermeier, JACM 2004
note: Vertex Cover has a 2k-vertex kernel in general; planar keeps a linear kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Alber, Fellows, Niedermeier, 'Polynomial-time data reduction for dominating set', JACM 51(3):363–384 (2004) — first linear kernel for planar dominating set
note: Linear O(k)-vertex kernel via region decomposition (bidimensionality). Poly kernel.

citation: Four Colour Theorem (Appel–Haken 1977; Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas 1997) — trivial 4k kernel; cf. bidimensionality linear kernels (Fomin–Lokshtanov–Saurabh–Thilikos)
note: Planar graphs have an independent set of size ≥ n/4, so if k ≤ n/4 answer YES, else n < 4k — a linear (4k-vertex) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: FPT: Chen, Liu, Lu, O'Sullivan, Razgon, JACM 55(5) (2008). Poly kernel is a well-known OPEN problem (as for Directed Feedback Vertex Set); noted open in Cygan et al. (2015)
note: Directed FAS/FVS is FPT but existence of a polynomial kernel is famously open — neither a poly kernel nor a no-poly lower bound is known.

citation: Farber, Hahn, Hell & Miller, Concerning the achromatic number of graphs, JCTB 40 (1986) 21-39 (FPT); Kolay, Panolan, Saurabh et al., Parameterized Reunion with Achromatic Number, ISAAC 2025
note: FPT parameterized by k (2^{O(k^5)}+O(|E|)). A polynomial kernel is known only on restricted classes (d-degenerate graphs, trees); for general graphs the poly-kernel question is explicitly stated open in ISAAC 2025. No coNP-based lower bound known.

citation: Basavaraju, Panolan, Rai, Ramanujan & Saurabh, On the Kernelization Complexity of String Problems, Theoretical Computer Science 730 (2018) 21-31
note: FPT by d (Gramm-Niedermeier-Rossmanith d^d). No polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, for the distance parameter d and any fixed alphabet of size >=2, via cross-composition. FPT algorithm exists but is incompressible.

citation: Fomin, Le, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, Thomassé & Zehavi, Subquadratic Kernels for Implicit 3-Hitting Set and 3-Set Packing Problems, ACM Trans. Algorithms 15(1) (2019) [SODA 2018]; earlier: Gramm, Guo, Hüffner & Niedermeier, Theory Comput. Syst. 38 (2005)
note: Deletion to a disjoint union of cliques = hitting all induced P3's (implicit 3-Hitting Set). Poly kernel; state of the art O(k^{5/3}) vertices.

citation: Guo & Uhlmann, Kernelization and Complexity Results for Connectivity Augmentation Problems, Networks 56(2) (2010) 131-142 [WADS 2007]
note: For augmenting to bridge-connectivity (2-edge-connected) and to biconnectivity (2-vertex-connected) by adding k links: problem kernel with O(k^2) vertices and links. Poly kernel.

citation: Bodlaender, Thomassé & Yeo, Kernel bounds for disjoint cycles and disjoint paths, Theoretical Computer Science 412(35) (2011) 4570-4578 [ESA 2009]
note: FPT by k (Erdős-Pósa). Disjoint Cycles has no polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, via composition + transformation from Disjoint Factors.

citation: Xiao & Kou, Kernelization and Parameterized Algorithms for 3-Path Vertex Cover, TAMC 2017, LNCS 10185, 654-668; general bound: Abu-Khzam, A kernelization algorithm for d-Hitting Set, JCSS 76 (2010)
note: 3-PVC = hit every P3 (a 3-element set) = 3-Hitting Set, so O(k^2) kernel follows; Xiao-Kou give a dedicated 5k-vertex (linear) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Bazgan, Chopin & Fellows, Parameterized Complexity of the Firefighter Problem, ISAAC 2011, LNCS 7074, 643-652; Bazgan, Chopin, Cygan, Fellows, Fomin & van Leeuwen, JCSS 80 (2014) 1285-1297
note: OFF-SCHEMA: this parameterization is W[1]-hard, even on bipartite graphs (Saving-k-Vertices). Not FPT unless FPT=W[1], hence NO kernel of any size exists -- kernelization presupposes FPT. The row's parameterized=FPT is inconsistent with its own canonical_task_param text. Flagged; does not fit the four-way FPT-kernel dichotomy.

citation: Mahajan & Raman, Parameterizing above guaranteed values: MaxSat and MaxCut, Journal of Algorithms 31(2) (1999) 335-354
note: Any CNF with m clauses has an assignment satisfying >= m/2, so k<=m/2 is trivially yes; a nontrivial instance has m<2k clauses, and each 2-clause has <=2 vars => <=4k vars. Linear kernel.

parameterization: excess above the tight (7/8)m guarantee, k
citation: Alon, Gutin, Kim, Szeider & Yeo, Solving MAX-r-SAT above a tight lower bound, Algorithmica 61(3) (2011) 638-655 [SODA 2010]
note: Satisfy >= (7/8)m + k clauses. FPT with a kernel of O(k^2) variables (fixed r=3) via the Fourier/algebraic above-average technique; poly(k) total size. Poly kernel.

citation: Bordewich & Semple, On the computational complexity of the rooted subtree prune and regraft distance, Annals of Combinatorics 8 (2005) 409-423
note: Rooted MAF is FPT by k; the subtree and chain reduction rules yield a linear kernel (O(k) leaves). Poly (linear) kernel.

citation: Zehavi, Maximum Minimal Vertex Cover Parameterized by Vertex Cover, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 31(4) (2017) 2440-2456 [MFCS 2015]
note: FPT parameterized by vc(G). No polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly, even on bipartite graphs (cross-composition).

citation: Gutin, Muciaccia & Yeo, (Non-)existence of polynomial kernels for the Test Cover problem, Information Processing Letters 113(4) (2013) 123-126
note: FPT by k. Parameterization 'a test cover with at most k tests' has no polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (cross-composition + parametric duality). A poly kernel exists only if test sizes are bounded by a constant.

citation: Cygan, Kratsch, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk & Wahlström, Clique Cover and Graph Separation: New Incompressibility Results, ACM Trans. Comput. Theory 6(2) (2014) [ICALP 2012]
note: FPT by k (Marx-Razgon; Bousquet-Daligault-Thomassé). Edge/Vertex Multicut parameterized by cutset size has no polynomial kernel unless NP⊆coNP/poly.

citation: Kratsch & Wahlström, Representative sets and irrelevant vertices, FOCS 2012 (poly kernel for BOUNDED #terminals, O(k^{s+1})); Wahlström, Quasipolynomial Multicut-mimicking Networks..., ACM Trans. Algorithms 18(3) (2022) [ICALP 2020]
note: FPT by s. A (randomized) polynomial kernel is known only when the number of terminals is a constant; for unbounded terminals only a quasipolynomial kernel is known. Existence of a polynomial kernel for the general (undirected) problem is open; the coNP lower bound of Cygan et al. covers only the DIRECTED variant.

citation: Jansen, Lokshtanov & Saurabh, A near-optimal planarization algorithm, SODA 2014, 1802-1811 (FPT); Jansen & Włodarczyk, Lossy Planarization, STOC 2022 (approximate kernel)
note: FPT (2^{O(k log k)} n). Vertex Planarization is NOT a Planar-F-Deletion instance (F={K5,K3,3} contains no planar graph), so the FLMS kernelization does not apply. Existence of a (true) polynomial kernel is a well-known open problem; only a constant-factor lossy/approximate kernel is known. No coNP lower bound established.

citation: Hanan (1966) + Dreyfus & Wagner (1971) (FPT via Hanan grid DP); cf. Dom, Lokshtanov & Saurabh, Incompressibility through Colors and IDs, ICALP 2009 (graph Steiner Tree by #terminals: no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly)
note: FPT by k. No polynomial kernel is known. The general graph Steiner Tree lower bound (Dom-Lokshtanov-Saurabh) does not transfer to the geometric rectilinear special case, and the Hanan grid yields a poly(k)-size PLANAR-GRAPH instance rather than a rectilinear kernel (and does not bound coordinate magnitudes). Neither a poly kernel nor a lower bound is established for the geometric version.

citation: Lokshtanov & Sloper, Fixed Parameter Set Splitting, Linear Kernel and Improved Running Time, ACiD 2005 (Algorithms and Complexity in Durham), 105-113
note: Max Set Splitting: a random 2-colouring splits >= half the sets, so k<=m/2 is trivially yes; combined with reduction rules this gives a linear (O(k)) kernel. Poly kernel.

citation: Sánchez-Arroyo, Determining the total colouring number is NP-hard, Discrete Math. 78 (1989) 315-319 (NP-hardness); Bodlaender, Jansen & Kratsch, Cross-composition, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1) (2014) [STACS 2011]; Drucker, New limits to classical and quantum instance compression, SIAM J. Comput. 44(5) (2015) [FOCS 2012] (AND-composition)
note: FPT by treewidth (Courcelle/MSO). No polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly, by AND-cross-composition: for a disjoint union tw = max_i tw(G_i) <= max input size, and χ''(union)=max_i χ''(G_i), so 'chi'' <= r' composes as AND from NP-hard Total Coloring. (Standard disjoint-union argument, same mechanism as q-Coloring-by-treewidth; derived, not a single named theorem for total coloring.)

citation: Fellows, Heggernes, Rosamond, Sloper & Telle, Finding k Disjoint Triangles in an Arbitrary Graph, WG 2004, LNCS 3353, 235-244; subquadratic: Fomin et al., ACM Trans. Algorithms 15(1) (2019)
note: Vertex-disjoint Triangle Packing = 3-Set Packing on the triangle hypergraph; crown-decomposition/3-Set-Packing kernelization gives O(k^2) vertices (subquadratic in later work). Poly kernel.
